title: From a generated spritesheet to a fully playable game
author: Neither_Finance4755
selftext:
Here's a quick video of my progress! Started out just messing around with a character spritesheet and a few background assets I generated. Finally stitched them all together and got a working prototype running. It's wild seeing all the static pieces actually come alive in-engine.

  
This was all made with [CanvasGPT](https://canvasgpt.com)

comments.author: Main-Lifeguard-6739
comments.body: Looks interesting! Was this done with pixijs? Canvas2d? Or something else?

replies.author: Neither_Finance4755
replies.body: Thanks! It's using Phaser under the hood for this particular game but it could have been done with any of those libraries if I asked it to, I personally like phaser as you can go pretty far with it using AI.

replies.author: Main-Lifeguard-6739
replies.body: and the canvas itself is also done in phaser? or is it only the game windows?

replies.author: Neither_Finance4755
replies.body: The canvas is a whole different architecture using Svelte and a bit of D3. The tile window is a hosted standalone web-app that can render html/js/css.

comments.author: some_CEO
comments.body: What’d you use to render the sprite sheets?

replies.author: Neither_Finance4755
replies.body: Spritsheet is generated on the canvas and rendered as a simple image node. The ai then embed it as a game asset automatically.
